To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the synthesis of N-acylneuraminic acids is blocked in all Morris hepatomas investigated, the activity of galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase is lowered, and the activity of ADPGalactose 3′-epimerases is elevated.
the activity of the key enzyme for N-acetylneuaminic acid synthesis is decreased in hepatomas, whereas the activity of the epimerase for galactose is raised.

in Morris hepatomas, the synthesis of sialic acid is decreased, the synthesis of galactose is decreased or unchanged, the synthesis of fucose is increased, whereas the catabolism of these sugars is generally increased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the metabolism of the terminal sugars of glycoproteins, namely L-fucose, D-galactos and N-acetylneuaminic acid, in liver and Morris rat hepatomas.
the regulation of the metabolism of the terminal sugars of glycoconjugate, especially of the sialyltransferases and fucosyl-transferases.

the regulation of the metabolism of free and membrane-bound carbohydrates and the synthesis of glycoproteins in normal liver and Morris hepatoma 7778, 3924 A and B, 5123 C, 5123 D, 5124, 5125, and 5126.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metabolism of terminal sugars of glycoconjugate in Morris hepatomas is altered in a characteristic way, which is in agreement with the altered carbohydrate pattern of the plasma membranes.

the metabolism of free and of protein-bound sugars is not significantly altered in hepatomas with short or intermediate growth rates; however, in fast-growing tumors the synthesis of glycoprotein-bound L-fucose is greatly increased, whereas the level and the activity of the enzymes involved in the biosynthesis of N-acetylheuraminic acid are decreased.
the terminal sugar metabolism in hepatomas is not altered to a great extent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the terminal fucosyl residues in glycoproteins are increased in hepatoma cells.
the synthesis of glycoprotein is not altered in Morris hepatomas.
in hepatoma cells the synthesis of fucosyl and sialyl residues is decreased, the synthesis of galactosyl residues is enhanced, and the turnover of fucosidic and galactosyl linkages is increased.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many different types of fucoproteins, and they can be used as biomarkers for cancer.
there are many different types of cancer, and they all have different causes.

the liver is the main site for the synthesis and metabolism of fucose, galactose and sialic acid in mammals and that the liver is also the main source for the synthesis and export of these sugars to peripheral tissues.
